It came with them, it says, as far as the place where the child was; / so it is plain that it came down into the depth like its Lord. / The King and his star came down into the depth to those below, / so that soul and body might rise on high to those above. / His star stood over the King’s door, as we have said, / and became like a lamp for the Magi to come in to him. / By its great light the offerings of the Magi came in / and were presented to the King of kings, who had come to his own. / They opened their treasures and presented their gifts to him: / gold and myrrh, and frankincense too, with discernment. / The newborn King was honoured by the envoys; / with offerings they worshipped him and turned back rejoicing. / And as they were about to go to Herod and tell him, / the night bound the road in sleep so that it would not be travelled. / The stillness of the night held the Magi back from going on, / and brought them to the place of dreams to teach them. / Subtly the teaching came in to instruct them, / so that not even in sleep would they be deprived of windows. / The dream came and plainly revealed the secret to them: / that Herod had laid a plot in secret against the King. / It taught them of his wickedness and what he had devised, / and what pretext he was stirring up against the child, should he find him.

It told them of his plot and the bitter thoughts within him: / he was preparing not to worship, but to kill. / It made them understand how he was lying in wait for the infant, / and that if he learned from them where he was, he would commit murder. / The king’s plot was exposed before the envoys, / and they mocked him, for he was fighting against the King of kings. / What the feeble king devised on his couch, / the dream went out and revealed plainly to the Magi. / The crafty one laid an ambush in secret, and no one perceived it, / but a vision of the night exposed his secret before many. / In the furnace of sleep the king’s false coin was exposed, / and the plot he had made was spoken of in visions. / By night, in its dream, it laid bare his hidden designs; / his secret came out, and the deed was left undone and went no further. / The king did not reveal what he devised even to his confidants, / yet his plot was exposed in a dream and became a laughingstock. / Though no one entered his palace or learned his secrets, / all his hidden things were proclaimed on the rooftops. / While guards held his doors with vigilance, / the word went out of the king’s house and they did not notice it. / A dream went out and brought out what was in Herod’s house,

and the crafty king was mocked before those from afar. / Through the revelation of the night, the stillness accused him, / and before the band of the Magi he was exposed. / The Magi changed their route and returned from the King’s house, / mocking Herod, who had schemed to deceive them. / By this very thing too the tidings of the Son were dawning / and being proclaimed on the roads of the whole world. / By one road they went up, proclaiming the King, / and going down again by another road they sang of his triumphs. / They filled the earth with new tidings by their words, / both going up to the King and coming down from him. / They told his story on the roads of the whole world, / for they went up by one and came down by another, meditating on him. / On two roads they spoke much of his kingship, / so that the earth might perceive him richly through their gifts. / The dream drew them onto another road and they went down, / and they heaped scorn on Herod, who had schemed to deceive them. / The crafty king was left wretched in his craftiness, / while the Son’s road was being trodden by the preaching. / A section suitable to be read at the Slaughter of the Infants, or else at the Commemoration of the Martyrs: / Then, after these things, the Watcher said to Joseph:

"Arise, take the Child and His mother, and go away to Egypt. / The king is about to stir up strife against the Child, / and the time has not yet come for Him to bear sufferings as is fitting. / Toward slaying and sacrifice His face is set, / yet not now, but at His own time, when it pleases Him. / He will receive the sword and the spear that come against Him, / but He will not die until He has completed the work of His course. / He is ready for death, but He will not drink His cup today: / arise, give place to the sword that is sharpened and lies in wait for Him. / He was not to bear the sufferings of sacrifice in secret; / He is sacrificed openly, before the eyes of many, to redeem them. / Not in an ambush does He come to death, like a weakling; / He is hung up on high, so that the worlds may see His might. / He was not to die mysteriously through the king's cunning; / the whole people shouts against Him and abuses Him. / He was not to become a sacrifice as a child in His mother's bosom; / on the top of the height He bears sufferings mightily. / Not secretly does He come to be slain by Herod; / before the eyes of all creatures He dies, and makes them tremble. / He flees today, not because He is afraid of Herod, / but to give place to cunning, so that it may not seek Him. / Let Him go and visit the land of Egypt gently,

and once the king's fury has abated, let Him return to Judea." / He goes to His own land, not to a foreign region; / He walks in what He Himself has sown, and all places are one to Him. / Joseph did as he was commanded by the angel, / and the One who carries all he carried to Egypt as a fugitive. / The Lord rode a light cloud, the Virgin full of strength, / to go down and visit the land of Egypt, which was sick. / He was borne upon a light cloud and went down / to the sick land that was darkened with idolatry. / The idols of Egypt saw the Savior and trembled before Him, / and shook before Him, as was proclaimed in prophecy. / The lion's whelp looked upon the foxes and terrified them, / and they were ready to fall before Him like weaklings. / The darknesses saw the great Light and hid from it, / and with His rays He pursued them out of the corners. / The ember of light put on a body and went out to the place, / to burn out from the lands the tares that were in it. / The pillars bearing the images of all Egypt trembled / before the One who had come to break them by His crucifixion. / All the stations of the altars were shaken / by the High Priest who had come as a sacrifice to abolish them. / Truth came in to do battle with the idols and shook them,

and though they had heard nothing of their fall, it summoned them. / And as these things were being spoken in truth / to the images of Egypt, which were mighty in worship: / "Fall, wretched ones, you who have long prevailed through oracles! / The Adored One has come; give Him place to stand in what is His own. / O carved images, make room for the Son of God! / Images of error, come down from the height of your temples! / Ruined idols, who became snares for your worshippers, / come down to be broken; hunt no longer to destroy. / Flee, weaklings, from the Mighty One who comes against you; / stand no longer in the place of the King, for behold, He has reached it. / Slaves who took the name of God and troubled the earth, / behold, the Maker has set out from His place to expose you. / A wind has gone out to sweep the thorns from the lands; / flee, tares, from the whirlwind, mistress of the ends of the earth!" / And the rust of idolatry shook before the Mighty One, / and the rows of images were broken in their fall. / The King went out over His lands, which had been laid waste, / and the Adored One began to make His paths level. / The Light went out to slay the darkness of the world, / and from every corner He hunted it out wisely. / To Babylon He sent a star of light to bring its hunters,

and He Himself went down to the land of Egypt, that it might be enlightened by Him. / On this side and on that He cast nets [?] into the whole world, / so that all creation might be gathered into the body of life. / Two regions that were bitter in their crafts / He began to visit, that by His teaching He might sweeten them. / The daughter of the Chaldeans He drew with a thread of light, and she came, / and He went down in His own person to visit the mistress of sorceries. / Magianism and sorcery He began to subdue, / so that all the bonds of iniquity might be loosed from the two of them. / He made a pretext for flight, fleeing from Herod, / and visited Egypt, whose bitterness was to be sweetened. / If it had not been fitting for Him to visit the land of Egypt, / why did He not then flee to Babylon with its envoys? / He set out on the way to one region by a star of light, / and fled to the other, to sow hope in both of them. / To the one He sent, and it came with offerings to honor Him; / the other He visited on His own feet, humbly. / To the one He showed might in His great rising, / to the other the humility of one who flees as a fugitive. / To one region He sent a star upon His visitation, / and toward the other place He set an ambush, for He fled, as it seemed. / The hosts on high ran along His ways,

and along the roads the light cloud carried Him in His flight. / He makes the cherubim tremble, and He trembled, as it seemed, and fled from a man; / He carries creation, and along the roads He was jolted about. / That justice might be done to His bodily state, He gave place, / until He grew to the stature of a man, and then He suffers. / He fled from the sword, not so as to escape it altogether, / but He waited so that His humanity might come to it. / He gave full stature to His sufferings when He set His face, / and therefore He fled from them while He was a child. / He kept the economy of His body, that it might not be confounded, / and to His upbringing He gave time to stand on its own. / Yet His visitation was not idle of good deeds, / for even while fleeing He was useful in what was His own. / In mercy He visited the sick land so that it might be healed, / and He called the gods of the place to be overthrown. / By His birth He went down to show it humility, / for it had been harsh toward the infants who were slaughtered. / To the land of Egypt, where Moses His servant was hidden, / He went to fulfil the type of the mysteries that had been drawn for Him. / But Satan was fighting alongside Herod / to cut off by the sword the King's course of good deeds. / The wicked one saw that the magi of Persia had mocked him,

and he grew embittered, so as to commit murders in place of the Child. / He saw that he did not know who the king was who was waging war with him, / and against the whole camp he decreed that he would destroy it all. / He thought that within the ranks the great general was hidden: / "I will lay waste to them all, and there he will die, and it will be known." / The head was hidden from him in the troop and did not show himself: / "Let it swallow them all, and behold, he is destroyed with his legions." / He had entered the band, and no one could tell him apart from the crowds: / "Let the sword go out, and with them he will die among the many." / The wretch did not know that he was waging war with the Mighty One, / who had gone off to visit another place and mock him. / The King had gone away to Egypt on His visitation, / and Herod remained, embittered over that visitation. / The lion's whelp was lying proudly in the thickets of Egypt, / and the contemptible fox was plotting toward his own destruction. / The eagle had gone and set his nest in the land of Egypt, / and the hawk of Judea raged against him to kill him. / The cunning king had laid an ambush, and it did not succeed for him, / and he began openly to raise up a side for battle. / He saw that he had been mocked by the envoys, who despised him and passed him by, / and he decreed to destroy also the King whom they had come for. / The tyrant king drew up battle against the Child,

and began to lay waste the infants of Zion, who had done no wrong. / He sent the sword against Bethlehem, the village of the King, / to kill all the children who were within its borders. / Those of two years and under were being killed, / according to the time that he had searched out and learned from the envoys. / For two years the magi had been coming to the land of Judea, / and when they were questioned by Herod they made this known. / From the time they received the rising of the King in the land of rivers, / in the second year they arrived at Jerusalem with their gifts of honor. / And when Herod began to lay waste the infants of the place, / he began to kill them from two years and under. / The tyrant waged a new war and became a laughing-stock, / for he called one-year-olds to battle in order to destroy them. / The lot of the infants was struck in the land of Judea, / and in place of the King who had come into the world they were being killed. / New martyrs they became for the Son as they were killed, / and by their sufferings they trod the way of the Son's slaying. / Beloved groomsmen who reached the Bridegroom's feast first, / they offered Him the first-fruits of blood from their necks. / Sons of the knife, whom the womb of sufferings bore, / to become laborers for the King Messiah by their wounds. / The sharp sword became their nurse and carried them,

and the bosom of the sword bore them and kept them. / The mothers wailed, who saw the sword upon their infants, / who by the command of the tyrant king were being killed. / The grandmothers lamented over their tender vines, still unripe [?], / for the boar had come in and trampled them upon their branches. / The fields of the house of Abraham wept with a thunderous voice, / for hail had come down and stripped off their blossoms. / The flocks of Isaac cried out in distress, / for the wolf had come in to tear its lambs, which were beloved. / A wail of sufferings was heard by the daughter of Jacob, / who saw her children being put to the sword by Herod. / Rachel was weeping, who saw her children, that they were no more, / and Jeremiah listened and heard her voice in revelations. / A voice in Ramah the prophet heard, of great weeping: / "Rachel is weeping, and will not, it seems, be comforted." / The congregation he named by Rachel, that daughter of Laban, / the mother of Joseph, whose father mourned over his wound. / The old man Jacob would not be comforted / so long as he supposed that Joseph had been killed by raiders. / Nor would the congregation turn to consolation / so long as it imagined that the King had been killed with the infants. / Egypt is accustomed to keep the saviors of the people safe,

and while they are thought to be slain, they live there. / Joseph was alive in Egypt, and mourning was made for him by his father, / who would not be comforted over his beloved. / There our Lord turned aside to flee from Herod, / and Rachel weeps that He has been killed, it seems, with the infants. / The prophet said to her: "Cease, for there is a reward for your tears," / as if one were to say: "The King is alive; do not grieve." / Behold, in Egypt is the treasure of plenty that comforts you, / the Lord of Joseph, who likewise gladdened his father there. / Hidden mysteries His descent into Egypt fulfilled, / for the Father called Him "My Son, out of Egypt" in prophecy. / And while the King was making His visitation among the Egyptians, / the infants of Judea were being killed on His account. / Herod let alone all the kings who were within his borders, / and against infants he drew up battle to fight. / The infants of Zion stood before him to hinder him, / and he brandished his sword against the fair ones and slaughtered them. / The wicked one laid waste the King's troop, but did not harm Him; / His company was swallowed up so that He might escape the knife. / The children drew up against Herod and fought with him, / and they conquered, for they did not hand over the general. / They raised up a side, and all of them died in the battle,

and they did not reveal where the King was, lest he swallow Him up. / O Herod, how the infants of the people have outwitted you! / What a disgrace it is to you that you fight with infants! / Do you boast of victory over sucklings? / Your side has been routed in the battle, for the King did not die. / The infants won the contest and defeated you; you will become a mockery, / for the head of the band was not destroyed by the knife. / The troops died, but the Bridegroom did not die, for it was not His time; / the guests were swallowed up, but the lord of the wedding came to no harm. / The Bridegroom had gone to invite Egypt to come with Him, / and the sword ruled over all His young men until He should come. / A wedding of blood He had come to celebrate in the land of Judea, / and the infants of the place were invited to be slaughtered. / The blood of the beloved entered the wedding in place of wine [?], / so that the whole wedding might blossom [?] in blood from its beginning. / Slaying was painted upon the feast in a mystery, / and whoever came to be a groomsman offered his blood. / A mystery went out and gathered grapes while they were still unripe, / and pressed from them new wine for the Bridegroom King. / The Virgin's Son invited virgin groomsmen for Himself, / that with virgin blood they might portray His slaying and sacrifice. / The fair ones were cut down for the Fair One, who had done no wrong,

to smooth the way for the pure blood that was to be poured out. / The king commanded that those of one year and those of two / who were within his borders—let the sword go out and lay them waste. / The sword was drawn for slaughter against the infants, / and without pity they were put to the sword wherever they were. / The command went out, and with it the sword, from Herod's house, / to search out the infants of the place and kill them. / Many were the questions about males from the slayers, / and with no mercy for their mothers they were killed. / The centurions of Herod's house went out through the place / and drenched the land with the blood of the young, which they poured out on it. / He brandished the sword over the bosoms of the women, / and emptied them of the fruits they were carrying. / The blood was poured out and filled the laps of the mothers, / and they died of fear, seeing the sword upon their beloved. / There was an infant who was sucking at the breast, and the sword caught him, / and with blood and milk it drenched the mother who held him. / There was one whom they beheaded in his sleep in his mother's bosom, / and from sleep he passed to death in a great stillness. / There was one whom they took from the knees of the mother who held him / and poured out his blood, and his sweet cooing was left behind. / Quiet martyrs, who did not speak while they were being slaughtered,

so that they might portray the great silence of Him who redeems all. / Simple ones, upon whom the sword came in to lay them waste, / and they did not know enough to ask: "The sword—what for?" / Little ones, who saw the light a little and had not had their fill of it, / when the sword of the fear of the wicked king took them away. / Contestants who did not speak while they were being killed, / but in silence were stretched out before the knife. / Confessors who showed deeds instead of words, / and without disputing set forth the account of faith. / Pure priests, who knew nothing at all of vestments, / and instead of incense brought their blood before God. / Choice lambs who were handed over to the knife, / and in silence were killed for the sake of the Shepherd. / Children against whom the sword rose up from the wicked, / and who were slaughtered in place of the King who came to His own. / Laborers who went out to clear the way of the crucifixion, / and from their sufferings watered it with the blood that befitted it. / Whole offerings, set apart from every blemish, / and in purity broken in place of the High Priest. / Envied ones, who had not provoked anyone in the land of Judea, / and yet the sword was drawn against them by the wicked. / Children who began to smooth His way through the world,

and the sword overtook them and scattered their limbs. / The infants died without knowing why, / but He knew it, for whose sake they were being killed. / Sons of the right hand of the newborn King, who stood with Him, / and bore sufferings for His sake from Herod. / Fire and the sharp sword went out and laid them waste, / for the sake of Him who had come to cast fire upon the whole world. / It was good for them that they suffered for His sake, / that they should be worthy to be neighbors of His birth. / The way of sufferings was laid down for Him to walk in, / and whoever came to be born with Him, the sword struck down. / Over the year-olds of His birth the sword held sway, / so that the way of blood might not cease from its journey. / Beloved children went out and trod it with their wounds, / until the King of sufferings should come to walk in it. / The infants of the place became slain hostages for the Son, / and He sent them to keep the place of the crucifixion. / To the place of death He sent them as they were killed, / that they might announce to it that the King is coming to the house of the dead. / And as these things were being spoken by the Savior / to the infants who went ahead on the way before Him to the crucifixion: / "Go and tell the tyrant king: Behold, I am coming;

and since you are in haste, you will call me to the place of your wickedness. / For I am coming on the way of sufferings that is laid down for me, / and I will loose you from the dominion of your wickedness. / I have a little time left to visit, since I was sent, / and after that I will come to you mightily. / You have greatly troubled humanity by your rebellion, / and behold, in the very humanity you defeated, I defeat you. / Make room for the living to enter your prisons, / for behold, I am coming, and the ranks you hold captive will go out. / Go, infants, wait there in the place of Sheol, / until I come and lay it waste of the dead. / Behold, in a little while I will reach you in the house of darkness, / and make a great light dawn upon you, that you may rejoice in it. / Go, wait for me within the darkness that is full of the dead, / and I will not delay; I will overthrow it, so that it shall not rise again. / Sleep away from the world, and rest from the couch [?] of all generations, / and when I have loosed it, I will awaken you along with many. / Go before me a little on the way of sufferings until I come, / and by crucifixion I will complete it, to raise you. / Go in and wait for me in [?] the great, the city of the proud, / and when I suffer I will cry out in it, and it will fall entirely. / Go into captivity with the many whom death has led away,

and behold, I am coming; I will break his bow and bring you back." / The infants mocked him by the sword while they were being killed, / for the way of the King was being trodden by their sufferings. / They laughed at death, for they did not know what its taste was; / for they did not complain when they were dragged to the knife. / The infants stood up, and were playing amid the slaughter; / the infants did not feel in death how bitter it was. / The sword wove a crown of infants from Bethlehem / for the adored King who came to die and to raise all. / As first-fruits they took their blood and brought it before Him, / that the holy blood might be honored with innocent blood. / May the slaying of the infants be to You, my Lord, a pure offering, / and by it be reconciled with the world, which stands in need of mercy. / Let peace hold the children of the Church that is held by You, / and drive away from it stumblings and schisms and division. / Seal with Your cross its high gates against contentions, / and let no turbulent enquiry from searchers enter it. / Let Your peace stand at its dark corners, / and let Your love mix its wine within it, that it may be sweetened by it. / Let Your peace be a watchful guard of its gates, / and whoever comes to tread its threshold, let him find peace. / Let the might of rulers be humbled by it,

and let it alone hold the earth with lordship. / Let it trample kings with the lofty heel of Your cross, / and bow down lords with the yoke of peace. / Let troops be drawn up in it for praise and not for strife, / and let the sound of alleluia rise from it, and not of quarreling. / Let the exalted who held regions bow down in it, / and let them sweep the dust from its threshold with their robes. / Let Your cross be a great standard over its building, / and let all the ends of the earth gather to it with their tribute. / Let it bend the strength of all kings by its sweetness, / and let it make the mighty of the world work at its tasks. / Let its little ones hold regions under their rule, / and to its authority let all authorities submit. / Let the lords of the world be servants obedient to it, / and let all lords kiss the dust of its feet. / Let its horn be raised over judges and their authorities, / and let heads and their regions be a footstool for its feet. / Let it hold the ends of the earth, and the kings of the world be its captives, / and let all the crowns of all rulers kiss its heels. / Let it lay its yoke on the shoulders of barbarians, / and in love set the cross as a collar [?] upon their necks. / Let it stretch out its ranks over the corners of the earth and seize them,

and hold all regions in Your name with authority. / Let it bend the strength of all the mighty beneath its threshold, / and let them come before it with their vows in plain sight. / Let it be mistress in the world over kings and judges, / and command them like servants concerning its affairs. / Let the bulwarks [?] of the earth be a footstool for its glory, / and let it set them to its service lovingly. / Let its peace increase, its assembly grow, its children exult; / let its horn be raised, its praise grow strong, its crown grow great. / Let its lap be filled, its enemies fall; let it trample its foes; / let its mouth be opened, its voice be raised; let it gladden the Watchers. / Let it forgive man, bind up diseases, heal pains; / let it be filled with virgins, exult in the perfect, rejoice in priests. / Seal with Your cross the Church and its children, who are chosen by You, / and let the turning of mercy reach me too, that I may be pardoned by it.
Here ends the homily on the star that appeared to the Magi, and on the slaughter of the infants.
On the baptism of the Law, on the baptism of John, and on the baptism that our Lord gave to the apostles

Again: Homily 7, on the baptism of the Law,
and on the baptism of John,
and on the baptism that our Lord gave to the apostles;
by the same Mar Jacob the teacher.

At the dawning of the Son, creatures that had been dark shone with light,
and the blind world, which had not been seeing, saw the light.
The ray of Being sprang up in the world and shone,
and like the day it drove the shadows from the corners.
Our Lord, the Light, showed himself among the darkness,
and the night that had covered the whole world fled away.
He sprang from the Father into the Virgin, the daughter of Abraham,
and began to walk the way he had laid down in the world.
In the virgin womb the Light dwelt in holiness,
and from there he began his way in the body.
He came forth from the womb and did not undo her virginity in his birth:
a new deed whose like had never been in the world.
He came forth into creation to uproot the thorns from the lands
and to sow peace in the earth that the great serpent had laid waste.

He came forth to renew the old things that had been corrupted,
and to establish on earth a new creation that will not be undone.
He became an infant who would play with the adder,
and he crushed the [?] that had bitten Adam among the trees.
From dwelling to dwelling he went down like a merchant,
laden with life to distribute among the dead.
He dwelt in that first dwelling, which is Mary,
and came to be born, so that as a human being he might visit the world.
The second dwelling, which is baptism,
he came and dwelt in, to put on armour for the battles.
John became a voice in the wilderness preparing the way,
and opened the door that brings people into the house of God.
Where there was water he stood like a fisherman,
to catch people by repentance for the new world.
John came to betroth a bride to the Son of God,
and he was making ready to wash her filth, and so she would be betrothed.
He brought her down to the water and cleansed her by repentance,
so that she might be pure and then see the King, the Bridegroom.
In the river he scoured her and took from her the shame of her face,
so that the Bridegroom, who loves beauty, would not see her filthy.
In baptism he made her pure and clear,
and so he brought her, holy, into the Bridegroom's chamber.

For this reason the son of the Levites ran to the river,
so that from within the water the bride might be full of beauty.
He washed her, scoured her, sanctified her,
and made her bright, so that the Bridegroom might see her beautiful.
He told her of the greatness of the King, his Lord,
and without ceasing proclaimed to her that he was heavenly.
He told her, "I am not worthy even of his sandals,"
so that by his humility he might magnify his Lord as he truly was.
The Bridegroom's sandals he loved more than his own head,
so that the bride might hear and be proud of the one to whom she was betrothed.
And as he proclaimed to her, he taught her that he himself was of the earth,
and of his Lord he taught her that he was heavenly.
Every day he kindled her with love for him, so that she would wait for him;
yet the Bridegroom was hidden, and the bride did not know who he was.
That he was great and glorious she learned from John,
yet Christ was hidden, and she burned with love to see him.
The crowds asked one another in great commotion,
"Where is he, where is he, the one whom John proclaims?"
And John was like thunder in his preaching,
and he cast the bride into love for the Son of God.

The crowds asked about him because he was hidden,
and baptism longed for holiness to overflow upon it from him.
Then the Bridegroom shone out like the sun and a great light,
and John was stirred to show the bride his beauty.
The Levite bowed and inclined his head in great amazement,
for he saw the Light, the Son of Majesty, who had come to him.
The Shoot of Being had dawned upon John,
and with his rays he urged her to marvel at him.
But the son of the Levites had never seen our Lord
in the body since his birth from the Virgin Mary.
While the Virgin was carrying him, he had seen him in his mother's womb
and received from him the Holy Spirit in a hidden place.
But when the Magi came to the Child, Herod was stirred
to kill the infants in Judea in his madness.
The Son of God fled from Herod to Egypt,
and the son of the Levites was hidden in the wilderness of Judea.
For when the children were being slain, Elizabeth took him,
the son of her barrenness, and went out in haste to the wilderness.
As for Zechariah, when the officers demanded
that he bring his son, they shed his blood at the holy altar.
So Elizabeth remained in the wilderness,
while John her son was raised by grace.

On roots, on leaves and on blossoms
he fed himself in the wilderness of Judea like the wild beasts.
He saw no settled life and no human food;
for thirty years he was raised in that wilderness.
He was reared under the care of the Holy Spirit,
with grace watching over him like a nurse.
Take note, you disciple, and see now
that John had never seen Christ at all.
This too was the providence of the house of God;
it took care, in the face of a people full of offence,
that they could not say he showed partiality to John
when he became a witness to the Son who was his friend,
or that out of affection and some arrangement made beforehand
they had made a pact that he would testify about him to help him.
Therefore he waited, not having seen him through the length of his years,
and the moment he saw him he showed the bride that this was the Bridegroom.
The Holy Spirit, the revealer of mysteries, filled him with radiance,
and by it he was stirred at the revealing of the Son of God.
He said to the bride, "This is the Bridegroom to whom you are betrothed;
this is that Lamb who takes away the sin of Adam.
This one does away with all the sacrifices of the sons of Levi,
for he himself, in his own person, becomes the sacrifice for sinners."

John trembled when he saw his Lord coming to him
and wishing to be baptized with the penitents in baptism.
The servant said, "My Lord, it is I who ought to be baptized by you,
for you are the sanctifier and the absolver of the whole world.
You give holiness to the priests, for you are holy,
and see, baptism looks to you to be sanctified by you."
Then our Lord silenced the servant so that he would not speak,
but so that he might fulfil .... [?] baptism.
"Permit it now; it is not the time to reveal the mystery,
lest the prince of the air perceive whose Son I am.
I do not want the demons to know whose Son I am,
until I bring him to the great hour [?] of the Crucifixion.
Be silent now and let me be baptized with the penitents,
so that the Accuser may be deceived and think that I am weak.
The way of birth has brought me to come to baptism;
and since I was born, see, I am being baptized: be still and baptize me."
John fell silent and kept the mystery as he had been commanded,
and the Bridegroom went down so that baptism might be sanctified by him.
The Son of the Rich One hid his riches in poverty,
so that like a poor man he might walk his way humbly.
John was silent, for he had been commanded to conceal the mystery,

and the Father spoke to reveal his Beloved to the crowds.
The Holy Spirit flew and came down upon the Only-Begotten,
so that the Father and the Spirit might be witnesses to the baptism.
The Spirit did not come down to sanctify the water so that then he might be baptized,
the holy Son, from whom holiness flows.
After Christ had bathed and come up out of the water,
the Spirit came down to show who he was, not to sanctify him.
For Christ did not come to baptism to be sanctified;
his way is plain to anyone who wishes to walk in it.
The baptism of John is one of repentance,
and it called sinners to be baptized so that it might absolve them.
But what sin or deficiency did Christ have,
that baptism should absolve him when he went down into it?
The Son of God did not become like us in sin,
that like a sinner he should be absolved in baptism.
And this is plain: though he had no need, he came to be baptized
so that the righteousness that is in the Law might be fulfilled.
He walked and came by the way of birth according to the Law,
and halfway along the way baptism met him upon it.
Had he passed it by and not gone down into it as he went,
he would have upset the order of the way on which he had set out.

And it would not be righteous for him not to complete the way as he had begun it;
so our Lord was baptized to pay righteousness its due.
He was baptized in water not to gain anything, nor to be sanctified,
but to fulfil that righteousness which is in the Law.
John, however, did not baptize with the Spirit and fire,
and his baptism did not give the Holy Spirit.
He baptized with water for repentance, as it is written,
and his baptism was poor for those who went down into it.
The Son of God gave his apostles his own baptism,
in which there is fire and the Holy Spirit for whoever goes down into it.
In it there is power, and it gives birth to spiritual children,
and because of their birth from it they call the Heavenly One "our Father."
New children, not mortal, it bears to the Father,
this baptism which the Son of God opened.
It is kindled with fire and Spirit and gives birth in a divine way,
so that from it human beings become children of God.
The Law, too, gave baptisms to the circumcised,
but they did not give the Holy Spirit to all who were baptized.
The Law commanded that whoever went in to see a dead body
should bathe in water and be unclean the whole day;
and whoever touched a bone of the dead should bathe in water,

and anyone defiled by an emission in the night should bathe as well.
On every occasion the Law gave baptisms,
to sketch a type of the baptism that gives birth to firstborn.
The baptisms in the Law were shadows,
and did not bring those who were baptized to perfection.
Greater than they is the baptism of the Son of God,
as much greater as the body is than the shadow.
Now, then, consider three measures
that there are in baptism for those who were baptized, as we have said:
one of the Law, another of John,
and the third, the one the Son of God opened.
The baptism of the Law is shadowy,
the baptism of John is one of repentance,
and the baptism of the Son of God gives birth to firstborn
and makes children who become brothers of the Only-Begotten.
Moses in the wilderness drew an image of baptism;
John opened it, so that it would be one of repentance;
and Christ came and kindled it with the Holy Spirit and fire,
so that it gives birth to new children, not mortal.
Moses the great, by his baptism, traced the outline
of the baptism in which the whole world is absolved.

John, for his part, scoured with it the filth of the sons of his people,
to sanctify them so that they might see the Son of God.
Then Christ came and opened baptism in his cross,
so that in place of Eve it might be the mother of life for the world.
Water and blood, in the likeness of spiritual infants,
flowed down to it, and baptism became the mother of life.
No baptism had ever given the Holy Spirit
except this one, which the Son of God opened in his side.
With water and blood it gives birth to children spiritually,
and in place of a soul the Holy Spirit is breathed into them.
They were not able to give the Spirit to baptism,
neither Moses nor John the son of the Levites.
The Son of God, from whom the Holy Spirit receives,
is the one who gave the Spirit, so that baptism might be sanctified by him.
And though he had no need, he came to be baptized by John,
with a baptism that was not perfect for those who went down into it.
John said, "I need to be baptized by you,"
and confessed openly how small his baptism was.
The one in need was urging the one with no need
to be baptized by him,
and it was made plain that our Savior was not baptized because he needed it.
John confessed openly that he was in need,

and the Son of God told him only to be silent,
so that he would not reveal his greatness to the crowds standing by;
he told him to permit it, so that baptism would not be made void.
But this baptism of repentance:
let us now see why it was opened by John.
This man had been appointed before the face of the Son of God
to go and prepare the way before his coming.
And so he began to call people to repentance,
to purify them and scour them clean of evil deeds,
so that the Son of God would find them holy,
blameless, and far from evil deeds.
And so he began to preach in the land of Judea
that the kingdom of heaven had drawn near,
as if to say, "The Son of God is near at hand;
flee from wickedness, for he greatly hates those who do wickedness."
John became the voice that cries, "Make the way level;
flee from wickedness, and come take refuge in repentance.
The King is coming: let the way on which he walks be prepared,
and let the straight miles of righteousness be set out along it.
Smooth, smooth the way for the Lord, for see, he has arrived,
so that he may find his people bright and pure."
So that the Son of God might come and see humankind

on a way full of righteousness and uprightness,
for this reason the Levite urged them on,
so that the sons of his people might show the fruits of faith.
And where the way was narrow, hard and rough,
he even called people "brood of vipers."
With threats and terrors and by every means
he strove to make people come to repentance,
so that the King's way might be smoothed of evil deeds,
and then the Son of the kingdom would be pleased to walk on it.
He bathed in water everyone who came to baptism,
and told them of the Savior, that see, he had arrived.
The daughter of the Hebrews was asleep when the Bridegroom came;
the sleep of wickedness lay heavy on her, and she did not perceive him.
But John, like a true friend and go-between,
woke her and told her that the Bridegroom had come.
Since she was filthy, he bathed her in baptism,
so that the Bridegroom would not see her in her uncleanness when she received him.
He brought her down to the river and washed her of the soot,
for [?] of the burnt offerings was on her face, and she was stained.
And he adorned her with fine garments as if in white,
so that she might stand beautiful in the bridal chamber of the Only-Begotten.

Between the Bridegroom and the bride a voice became the herald,
so that the bride might perceive the procession of the Bridegroom who was arriving.
As if to say: between mouth and ear the voice
escorts the word, so that it comes in procession to the hearing.
The voice resounds in an empty place to show itself,
for it has no place either in a bosom or in a chamber.
So John, too, who is a voice in an empty place,
that is, the wilderness, resounded, and the crowds of Judea heard him.
The Levite sang, and at his songs the bride rejoiced,
and the wilderness thundered with the tidings of the Bridegroom King.
The groomsmen gathered and awaited the Son of the kingdom,
and the bride bathed and sat in awe, watching for him to come.
And when our Lord dawned like the day upon the darkness,
the voice was stirred at the dawning of the Word to speak.
It showed the bride, the daughter of the shining ones, to whom she was betrothed,
and the Father became a witness to his Son with a loud voice.
The Father by a voice became a witness to his Only-Begotten,
and the Holy Spirit showed himself beside the Savior.
In the likeness of a dove he flew and came down perfectly,
after the vessel of baptism had bathed and come up.
He waited to show, so that it became plain that our Lord had no need
for baptism to be sanctified for him first and then for him to bathe.

When he came up out of the water, the Holy Spirit
led him, and he went out from among the crowds to the wilderness.
The bride saw the Bridegroom who had come and knew who he was,
and at once he went out to wrestle with the Wicked One.
He left the bride, who knew him and was proud of him,
and went to do battle with the ruler who guards the air.
He set his face to make war with the Archon,
and, once he had overthrown him, to come and show the bride his riches.
Against the one who had taken humankind captive from the Father's house
he set his course, and only then did he shine forth in the assemblies,
so that when he had been tempted and had made war, and had struck him down and he had fallen,
he might show himself in the mighty works he did valiantly.
When the fall of the Adversary had come like lightning,
then the Son of God began to work signs.
The bride knew who the Bridegroom was, but he did not wait
for her to rejoice with him; he went out to wrestle,
to strike down that rebel who had taken the bride captive,
out of his dominion, and so to take for himself the daughter of day.
The Spirit led him to be tempted and to make war,
and in victory to show himself in the assemblies.
He fought the contest, and the Adversary fell like lightning,
and then he began to walk the way of mighty works.

The whole way of the Only-Begotten is full of wonder;
blessed is the Dawn at whose coming all creation shone.

Here ends the homily on the baptism
of the Law, on the baptism of John, and on the baptism that our Lord gave to the apostles,
composed by the blessed Mar Jacob.
On the baptism of our Savior in the Jordan

By the same holy Mar Jacob:
Homily 8,
on the baptism of our Savior in the Jordan.

Christ the Bridegroom made a wedding feast for the congregation of the peoples,
and the world took notice of the feast He had prepared for her.
The Son of the kingdom wished to betroth the one who had been tossed about,
and He sent her to go to the spring to wash away her filth.
He saw the persecuted one, who was weak, faint and weary,
and He mixed water and sent her to bathe, and so be betrothed.
He looked on her beauty, which had been marred by the smoke of idols,

and He made rays of light shine on her face, that her complexion might grow fair.
To the chosen waters He first brought her down as He betrothed her,
so that by holiness He might scour harlotry from her.
The reek of [?] from the sacrifices that clung to her grieved Him,
and He poured pure waters over her, that her body might be fragrant.
She had grown foul from the filth of the burnt offerings,
and He sprinkled holiness on her, that by it she might be cleansed of uncleanness.
In the bosom of baptism He laid a robe of glory,
and sent the bride to go down and put it on from within the waters.
He called His true one, the son of barrenness, and sent him before Him
to go and bring adornment to the bride until He Himself should come.
John went out bearing the riches of the great treasury,
to adorn the daughter of the poor, as he had been commanded.
He took and opened the bosom of the Spirit above the waters,
and brought out garments, that the Church might put on holiness.
He showed her wondrous garments that she had never seen,
which had been prepared on that loom of the house of God.
He captivated her with his wondrous [?], laden with promises,
as he proclaimed to the daughter of beggars the kingdom on high:
"Behold, the kingdom has drawn near to you, the kingdom of heaven;
the Bridegroom has set out to come to you, that you may be united with Him."

He called the maiden, and she gave herself to listening,
for she had learned that the Bridegroom was a King who was coming to her.
She called Isaiah, to learn from him about John:
"Who is this who announces to me the kingdom on high?
Come, prophet, come and explain the herald to me,
for I need to learn from you the truth.
I accept that voice of yours which spoke on my behalf,
for I heard the word of your message long ago.
You made me trust in the reward by your prophecy;
come, see whether the time has come for me to enter.
See what manner of man this is who proclaims precious things,
while poverty itself is seen in him.
His appearance is shabby, yet rich is the voice of his proclamation;
his garb is mean, yet great is his word in the ears of all.
The man does not speak to the measure of what I see in him,
nor is the promise he sows in my ears lowly like himself.
He makes his words great though he owns nothing at all;
he wanders in the desert and announces to me the kingdom on high.
Tell me plainly whether he is true, that I may listen to his words,
and if he is not true, that I may not be led astray by him as by the rest.
Your Lord is coming, and I am making ready to enter before Him:

reveal the truth to me, and do not leave me beside a deceiver."
Isaiah drew near to teach the Church about John:
"He is the son of the mystery of the Bridegroom, your Lord; receive his words.
This is the voice that cries in the wilderness before the King's Son:
'Clear, clear the way for the Lord in faith.'
Go, go down and bathe; do not question the herald;
the wise one is clearing the way to make it straight for the King who is coming."
The Church, the bride of the King, drew near to John,
and he began to wash, cleanse, polish and sanctify her.
He was faithful to her, and toiled over her adornment as much as he could;
he taught her wisdom, to be modest, since she was betrothed.
She heard his voice and was drawn after his words, and supposed
that he was the Bridegroom to whom she was betrothed.
She held fast to the servant lovingly, as though he were the Lord,
because Christ was hidden from her among the tribes.
The true one saw that the betrothed bride was clinging to him,
and he began to shake out his bosom and cry, "I am not the Bridegroom."
He pushed her away from him so that she would not go astray over him, since he was a servant,
and as he withdrew, he hung her hope on the Bridegroom.
He humbled himself: "I am not worthy even of His sandals,"
so as to keep the lordship for his Lord, as a true servant.

He saw that the maiden had let her eye rest on the Nazirite,
and he hastened to cut off from her mind every occasion of stumbling.
He bound her by his words to wait for the Bridegroom and not to gaze at him,
proclaiming to her, "After me He comes, and He was before me."
She began to watch for when she would see Him coming to her,
examining the baptized one by one.
She cast her eye about to look among the many,
that among them she might see the Only One to whom she was betrothed.
Whenever anyone went down to baptism, the crowds surrounded him
to examine him, whether perhaps he was the Christ who was to come.
The Church gathered and stood in the desert beside John,
watching with the wedding guests to see which one was the Bridegroom.
She surrounded the river and cast her eyes among its waves,
to receive the Betrothed of truth from within the waters.
She stood, beautiful, looking for the Bridegroom, for when He would come,
that she might enter with Him into the bosom of the waters to be sanctified.
Her wing spread wide, she waited for Him around the waters,
so that when He bathed she might receive Him in holiness.
John too was waiting for when He would come,
that his baptism, which was lacking, might be made complete in Him.

He was keeping the secret that lay between him and the Father,
and watching for the Spirit, that it would testify to the True One.
Even as he laid his hand on those who came, to baptize them,
he kept looking upward because of the word he had been given there.
He fixed his eyes on the many who were with him,
to see whom the Spirit would point out when it was sent.
He watched for that winged one, the lady of the heights,
how she would descend, and on whom she would rest to bear witness to Him.
He waited for the swift wings that bear up the farthest bounds,
to see whom they would receive from within the waters.
He longed to see the wing that flies without fluttering,
that when it appeared it might be a witness to the Savior.
He listened for that daughter of the Father's gentle voice,
to hear from her over whom she would cry, "This is My Son, My Beloved."
The bride stood beside the true one, the son of barrenness,
and waited for when he would signal, "This is the Bridegroom."
She watched him, that he might show her the Savior,
and he awaited the Father, that He might testify to His Beloved.
Whenever anyone came to go down and be baptized, she pressed close to him,

in case he was the Bridegroom, that she might receive him lovingly.
He said to the crowds, "Behold, among you stands the Bridegroom,"
and this voice set the bride on fire and kindled her.
He proclaimed again, "I am not worthy even of His sandals,"
and again he set her ablaze with love of Jesus and His exaltedness.
The bride of light hastened and stood beside John,
so that when he showed her which one was the Bridegroom she might fall before Him.
On everyone who was led forward to come and be baptized,
the bride's eye was fixed until he came up again.
Thousands were baptized, and there was no Spirit descending on them;
myriads bathed, and the river was cold, without the brooding Spirit.
Crowds went down, and the waters were ordinary, as they always are;
many came up, and the Father's voice was hidden as before.
And when the bride had been made complete in the ornaments of repentance,
she bathed and came up from within the waters of baptism.
And when the whole wedding was ready with all its adornments,
only the Bridegroom held back from coming to do His part.
The washing served the guests and cleansed them,
but garments of the Spirit were not put on from within the waters.
All the peoples stood there stripped,
waiting for the Bridegroom to come and clothe them.

And when the bride's filth had been washed away in the waters and she had come up,
everyone looked for the white robes that the Bridegroom would bring.
And while baptism still lacked forgiveness,
and no one had received the Holy Spirit from the waters,
and while the whole feast was looking for the Bridegroom, wondering where He was,
the King's Son came out from among the crowds to come to the river.
While He was still far off, baptism stirred to meet Him;
the river overflowed and proclaimed Him in silence.
The Holy Spirit went forth from Him and stood upon the waters,
and the warmth of His might kindled them.
His fire licked among the waves before He went down,
and the river leapt with a great surge of flame.
Baptism yearned for Him who had come to it,
as that horn of anointing yearned toward David.
It was not to sanctify Him that it stirred to meet the Holy One,
but that its own bosom might be sanctified by its Beloved, indeed [?].
It rejoiced in Him, for He was its perfecter and its seal,
and it spread its wing of holiness that it might receive the Son in it.
John saw the river seething and its waves churning,
and he knew that the Holy One had come to baptism.

He drew back his hand so as not to baptize those who were coming,
that Christ the Bridegroom might be revealed and stand alone.
He cried out to the crowds and made them flee from beside the river,
that everyone might know why baptism was stirring.
He drove the flock back, that it might move away from the spring,
so that the Lamb of sacrifice might come forth, set apart from the pasture.
He signaled to the wedding guests, and they made room for Him among the crowds,
that the Bridegroom might be shown in glory to all the peoples.
The crowds that had gathered around baptism fled,
and the Son of the kingdom stood alone, unique.
The true one ran to tell the free woman about the Savior;
he called the modest one to show her that He was her Lord:
"To this Bridegroom I betrothed you, O Church, from the beginning;
you have hung your hope on Him since you came.
This is the Lamb who offered Himself to be a sacrifice;
this one takes away the sin of the world by His slaying.
In this very one I made you trust, from long ago;
in His name I seated you to wait for Him.
For Him I kept you with care, as a true servant;
acknowledge to Him for me that I did not let you be stolen away by me."

And while the King's bride was being instructed by John,
behold, David, the harp of the Spirit, drew near and sang to her:
"Hear, my daughter, and see, and incline your ear to praises,
and forget your people and your father's house, for they are estranged.
Truly He is your Lord: draw near and worship Him;
do not be divided over the Savior who has come to you."
The Church learned from John and also from David,
and she was assured that He was the Bridegroom to whom she was betrothed.
She drew near and stood to see how He would be baptized,
so that when He came up from the waters she might fall before Him.
Christ drew near to John to be baptized by him;
John saw Him and drew back his hand from the Fiery One.
He bowed his head before the Son, saying to Him,
"It is I who ought to be baptized by You, for You are holy.
I was watching for You, so that I might hand baptism over to You quickly;
here is Your treasury: release me now, that I may rest a little.
It was a post I was keeping, for the lordship is not mine;
take Your own rank; I have no authority over Your domain.
A king does not receive authority from a beggar;
from his crown go forth the ranks of all authorities.
What does baptism have that is not Yours,

and what do You lack, that You should go down and take it from within the waters?
If forgiveness flows from You to mankind,
and if remission is Yours, then so is the remission of sins.
If all priesthood is in You, for You are the High Priest,
and if You are the kingdom, You who bind crowns on kings,
then holiness flows from You to mankind,
and if it is priesthood, behold, the world stands at Your right hand.
Since the fullness of the Godhead is with You,
what does a little river have, that it should bring You to completion?"
Our Lord said, "I lack nothing but one thing:
the finding of Adam, who is lost to Me, is what I seek.
Let Me go down to seek Adam, the beautiful image,
and when I find him, all My will is fulfilled.
I have searched greatly on his track, and for this I came,
and if I do not find the lost one, that is a lack.
This alone I lack: to find him with Me,
that I may gain Adam, whom the Evil One wished to be lost from My hands.
By this finding My will comes to completion,
for Adam is what I lack, that he may enter into his inheritance.
Let Me, then, go down to cleanse the image that was corrupted,
so that he too may not be lacking if you hold Me back.

That goodness which called Me to come to birth
is the same that now calls Me to come to baptism as well.
Great mercy drew Me down to become a babe;
it is the same that drew Me down to be baptized.
The bosom of baptism is no narrower than the womb,
nor are the river's waters darker than the stall.
If you think that you are sparing My honor,
you should have held Me back from the womb and from birth as well.
If it is a disgrace to Me, which is the more despised place:
the womb of flesh, or the greatness of baptism?
If you had held Me back from coming to the womb while you were in your mother,
it would be clear that you should forbid Me to be baptized as I was sent.
If you had turned Me back from that step of birth,
then come, turn Me back from the order of baptism.
If you had made Me pass by the swaddling bands, so that I was not wrapped,
then drive the river's waves away from Me, that they may not cover Me.
If you had stopped Me from sucking the despised milk,
you might hold Me back from the spring, so that I do not go down to it.
If you had prevented Me from dwelling in Mary's lap,
I would pass by the bosom of baptism as well.
But now that I have walked and come along the way of those who are born,
I must complete it; how can I turn back from it?

For thus too it befits Me, since I was sent,
that the whole way on which I came down be fulfilled in Me."
John trembled, shook, and was terrified before the King's Son;
he worshipped Him and confessed, pleading in a voice like thunder:
"I beg You, my Lord: I am not fit to draw near to You;
feeble is the straw that would lay its hand on the coal.
How can stubble take hold of a flame,
or a dry twig lay its hand on embers?
The heat of Your might has licked the river, and behold, it is burning;
how is it, then, that You do not scorch hands of flesh?
Nor is it fitting that You be baptized by me as one who lacks,
lest there be a breach in the world, saying that You are lacking.
Go, Son of the King, redeem the captive people who are waiting for You;
You have no need to take armor from within the waters.
Your crown is Yours from eternity and does not change;
You are not filled from the treasury of baptism.
Hasten on Your way; behold, the exile thirsts to see You;
You are not looking for anyone's escort to go with You.
In the Father's purple You were born from His being,
and You have no need to put on anything here before You save.
Do not delay the battle on earth for the sake of redemption:

go forth, rescue the captive peoples from the persecutors.
The kingdom of the Father and Yours is one, Lord of kings;
it is not from here that You gain strength for authority.
Behold, exile has overrun peace; why do You stand still?
Run, bring her back from the stumblings by which she went astray.
Behold, raiders have plundered her; speed Your course to the place;
go forth, bring back the captives who were carried out of Your dominion.
Baptism has nothing to add to what is Yours,
so why then do You hurry to go down and bathe?"
"Be still, John; you add nothing to Me;
the waters need the brooding Spirit, that they may be filled from Me.
It is not to receive a reward that I go down to the spring,
but to forge great armor for those who do battle.
To burnish mankind in this generation I hasten to the battle,
so that whoever comes to the contest may draw near like Me.
I am making baptism into an armory,
so that whoever goes in and puts on armor from it will not be beaten.
If I pass by and am not baptized, as you would hold Me back,
no one can take armor from within the waters.
Like a commander of the army I will take the lead in the contest,

that I may be an example to the hosts who come after Me.
And if I turn aside from the way that I have trodden and come,
they too will pass by after Me, as they have seen Me do.
And if My soldiers are not made strong from within the waters,
they will not meet the great battle like valiant men.
Though I have no need of the furnace of the waters, behold, I enter it,
that in that mold of Mine worn-out mankind may be recast.
I entice them to come to the spring as I did,
that they may be stamped spiritually with My coinage.
I bring men down to the grave of the waters,
that in the resurrection I may make them immortal.
I bring them into the desirable womb, that it may conceive them,
and that without pangs a new birth may bear them.
And if it is purity, I will be baptized by you; do not delay.
Come, open the way, for the world is watching to be renewed in Me."
The [?] one drew near to the Mighty One and asked Him,
"How, my Lord, is there a way for this to happen?
To the bride of light who is betrothed to You, I said this:
'With the Holy Spirit and fire the Bridegroom, your Lord, baptizes.'
Behold, she is watching for You to baptize her, as I taught her;
how, then, shall she now draw near and see that You are baptized by me?

I confessed before her that I am not worthy even of Your sandals,
and how shall I dare to lay my hands on Your head?
In Your name I was baptizing her, that she might be adorned with You,
and You, the Holy One, I do not know in whose name I am to baptize.
Behold, my words are lodged with her, and she holds to them,
for I told her, 'He baptizes you with the Holy Spirit.'
How, then, shall I now go back on my words and change my voice,
and baptize You altogether like the rest, in water?
I shall be counted a liar, and You will be made small,
and the bride will think there is poverty in her Betrothed.
What shall I say when I baptize the Forgiver of sins,
and with what words shall I keep the order of baptism?
Shall I baptize the Son in the name of the Father? Behold, You are in His bosom,
and there is not even the gap of a small sign between You and Him.
Shall I invoke the Son? You alone are the one who sanctifies the waters,
and since You are holy, why should You wash Your holiness in baptism?
If I baptize You in the name of the Spirit, how can it be
that I seal the waters separately, when You are one with the Spirit?
The Father is in His Child, and the Son is wholly in His Father,
and the Spirit is from Him, one dominion without confusion.
How, then, shall I, weak clay, do this,
and cast a breach into that harmony which is not divided?"

"Leave your questions, John, and be at peace;
at this hour, do not concern yourself with these things.
It is not that baptism may sanctify Me that I have come to it,
nor is there any need for you to say anything when I am baptized.
Silently, only lay your hand on My head,
and as for what belongs to the Father, He will say what He says of His Child.
Stretch out your right hand, for it comes to Me only as a loan,
and without your word the Spirit bears witness to the True One."
And while the son of barrenness was in fear over these things,
he then allowed the Son to be baptized according to His will.
He drew near trembling, worshipped confessing, reached Him shaking;
he quaked and was terrified, and strength upheld him so that he would not fall.
The Holy One came and reached the waters to go down and be baptized,
and His fire licked among the waves and set them ablaze.
The river leapt in the pure bosom of baptism,
as John leapt in Elizabeth toward his Lord.
The waters were turned to coals by flashes of flame,
for living fire had come to baptism to bathe in them.
The Kindler of worlds cast His coal upon the spring,
and its heat set the river ablaze with holiness.
The plain waters were made to gleam like glass by the rays of holiness,

for grace had gone forth from the Holy One and set them ablaze.
The ember of fire came down to bathe among the waves,
and there kindled the burning of its holiness.
The coal came and lifted up the garments it had put on,
and came down to cast fire into the waters of baptism.
The Watchers marveled at that washing of flame,
as its bright body quivered to sanctify the waters.
The waves of the waters were mingled with rays,
and the river was dazzled by the splendor that dwelt in it.
The vault of the waves was beaten by the currents,
and flashes of flame surrounded it on every side.
Amazement and great wonder fell on all creatures,
as the Coal came down to be baptized by John.
The whole air grew hot and was set ablaze with holiness,
for the Son of the Holy One came down to baptism, though He lacked nothing.
The Spirit was mightily set ablaze with fire,
that in brightness it might receive the Bridegroom from within the waters.
Beautiful glory blazed forth from every side,
and made a procession for the Son of the kingdom with honor.
Clouds of light flew from the ends of the earth and stood there,

to be a bridal canopy for the glorious Bridegroom who had come down to be baptized.
Thick clouds went forth like the curtains of the royal palace,
so that when the King's Son had bathed He might be received in them.
The Father spread out choice furnishings above the air: splendor
and glory and flashes of wonder, and thick clouds as well.
He surrounded the river with wondrous colors that cannot be touched,
to exalt the wedding of His Only-begotten Son.
He split the heavens and raised His voice mightily:
"Behold, this is My Son; this is My Beloved, truly."
The Spirit flew from the Father's side with great wonder;
it flew, came down, alighted, and abode upon His Beloved.
It came in the likeness of the form of a dove, perfectly,
to nest there and build its nest in baptism.
It put on the form of a dove, the choicest of birds,
and came to bear witness to the True One in its simplicity.
It was not to sanctify the Son that it came down when it was sent,
for the adored Word had no need of it to sanctify Him.
It did not sprinkle holiness on the Holy One by its descent;
it bore witness to the Savior when it appeared.
The Spirit became a finger for the Father, and with it He pointed:
"This is My Son; do not be divided over His coming."

If the Spirit had not come down upon the True One,
who would have known where the Father's voice was resting?
Together with the word that was cried out from on high,
the Spirit pointed out, as if with a finger, that this is the King.
For had it not rested upon him for all to see,
the voice would have wandered among the crowds over many.
They heard the voice that said, "This is the Beloved,"
and, divided among themselves, they asked about whom it had spoken.
The Spirit came down to rest upon him in holiness,
not because he lacked holiness and was then filled with it.
The Law, too, calls for two witnesses together,
for one alone is not accepted, however truthful he is.
The Father and the Spirit bore witness alike to the Only-begotten,
so that by the Law they might give the verdict to the one True One.
The Father's voice and the Holy Spirit came down together,
so that no one should reject their testimony once it had appeared.
The Father's voice split the heavens and came out from them,
and stood over the river, that boundless sea of light.
The Spirit set out and came on her wings with great glory,
and the wilderness was flooded with the radiance that poured from on high.
The Church, the bride of light, marveled at the Bridegroom King,

in whose bathing height and depth were made level.
She saw the river with its trembling streams, all ablaze,
and she heard the Father's voice crying out over his Beloved.
She sent for that harp of the Spirit, David,
to come and sing strains fit for the wedding feast:
"Come, son of Jesse, and bring your songs with you,
so that at the feast of your Lord and your Son we may rejoice today.
Polish your melodies and tune the strings of your lyre,
and raise strains that will gladden me plainly.
Do not speak to me in symbols as you sing;
bring out your word, and let truth thunder in your songs.
Tell me openly, explain to me, why the river trembles,
and what power pressed upon the deep, so that it shook and was dismayed.
What is this voice coming down from the height to the depth,
and why these flashes of fire that have set the air ablaze?"
David raised strains of praise before the Bridegroom,
to explain to the Church the event just as it had been:
"The waters saw you, O God; the waters saw you and were afraid;
the deeps also shook, and the clouds of the air poured down water."

"All the nature of the waters perceived that you had visited them:
seas, deeps, rivers, springs and lakes.
They pressed upon one another to be blessed by your footsteps,
for your great Epiphany that came upon them made them rush.
You trod upon the Jordan as upon the head of all the seas,
and at your might the heels of the deeps and the floods shook.
All the nature of the waters was stirred by your brooding,
for by your baptism you made them all worthy of pardon.
The waters of the seas, though far away, were not far,
for the power of your holiness drew them secretly and visited them.
Therefore the waters saw you, saw you and were afraid;
the deeps also shook, for by your descent you made them rush.
The clouds sprinkled water into the river while you were being baptized in the water of the river,
so that they too should not be deprived of your brooding.
Behold, the heavens also gave voice through your Father on high,
so that by his testimony the earth might perceive that you are the Only-begotten.
Your lightnings lit up the world, and it saw a splendid light,
for the earth had been troubled in darkness until it came.
The waters saw you and feared you as their Lord,
for the blast of your strength made them boil as you came down."
David explained the cause of the event as he sang,

and Zechariah came and called the Church to show her:
"Here is the man of whom I told you, whose name is the Dawn;
see, he has shone forth, and the ends of the earth are lit by his rays."
John drew near and laid his hand upon the live coal,
and the ranks of the Watchers drew back all around in terror.
The hosts were astonished at the wonder they saw,
as the straw met the coal and was not scorched.
The heavenly beings marveled at the fearful sign that took place there,
that a hand of flesh was not harmed by the flame.
Seraphim cover their faces from his coal,
yet a hand of moulded clay was laid upon his head.
A brick shaped from earth took hold of the sea,
and laid its hand upon the flood and was not dissolved.
It is a wonder to tell: while the fiery beings owe him homage,
he went down to baptism by the right hand of a son of barrenness—
he who is borne by the cherubim, exalted in the chariot, hidden from the Watchers,
concealed from the ranks, praised by the hosts, feared above the legions.
The ranks cover their faces, the hosts are hard pressed, the orders are terrified,
the armies tremble, the troops quake, the thousands shudder.
The flame stands aside as though trembling,
and he went down to be baptized by the dust his hands had formed.

The heavens split, and the Father cries out over his Beloved;
the Spirit shines and stands to bear witness to the Only-begotten.
A voice came out from the chamber of the royal palace
to vouch for the King's Son, that he was no stranger.
The hidden Word was stirred, though not from a mouth,
to go out and bear witness to that Child of the Godhead.
That daughter of the voice, hidden from all, was revealed,
crying out concerning that Hidden One who had come to be revealed.
A lofty voice with no tongue thundered in heaven:
the Bodiless One [?] spoke over his Beloved, who had taken a body.
He did not speak through an angel at that time,
nor did he proclaim it by the sent mouth of one of the Watchers.
He did not borrow word or voice from the heavenly beings,
for he spoke from his own being about his Only-begotten.
The Father spoke in his own person, truly,
to vouch for his Child, that he was true.
A new word was heard among the crowds,
a lofty voice whose like was never spoken again.
A melody never before sown in human ears,
a fearful thunder, sounded its voice once alone.
He never spoke such a word at any other time,

for he had no other child anywhere at all.
The Mighty One thundered to show his love for his Son among the crowds,
to make known to them that he had this true Son.
The compassion of fatherhood was stirred over the Only-begotten,
and [?] pressed it to show that he was its beloved.
The Godhead, exalted above all, was not ashamed
to see its Son clothed in a body and bathing in the waters.
That majesty was not diminished when its Beloved
went down to the baptism that was reckoned as redemption.
His lack was not being made up by the waters,
so that the Father should disown him and not acknowledge him because he was lacking.
He was perfect before he went down, as also after he went down,
and the Father could boldly acknowledge his Son.
This was the reason that called him to come to baptism:
that the hand of the priests might reach its end in him and pass on from him.
The Father had given a deposit to Moses on the mountain,
and he sent his Son to receive it in the waters from John.
It had been carried down upon that tribe of the sons of Levi,
and the lion's whelp of the house of Judah arose and took it from it.
Holiness had flowed down upon Mount Sinai from on high,

and through John it was poured out upon our Savior.
From his beginning our Lord undertook to complete his course,
so as not to go round by another path like a stranger.
That priesthood which had been carried down from the house of Aaron
went out from our Savior through the apostles to the world.
It was not because the great High Priest of priests was lacking
that he took it at baptism and then gave it;
rather, so as not to confuse the path of truth that his Father had laid out,
he himself brought renewal to the things of old.
It is not because the ocean lacks anything of its fullness
that all the streams and rivers pour themselves into it.
The nature of the waters runs to the sea, though it lacks nothing,
and the whole sea grows no larger than it is.
It was not because Christ was in need that he received the hand of Aaron,
nor because he lacked anything that he took the kingship from the house of David.
Kingship flowed down with priesthood and came to rest upon him,
since he is the High Priest and the King of kings.
Holiness flowed and came and fell upon him,
like a channel into the full sea, which lacks nothing.
Kingship came from the house of David and was poured out upon him,

though in kingship he was far richer than the sea.
He came up just as he had gone down, holy, as he is,
and was received on the wing of the voice from his Begetter.
The Spirit encircled the baptized Bridegroom with wings of glory,
and the Church was assured that it was he, and fell down before him:
"O Perfect One, who came to make up in the waters what was lacking,
let your great grace flow out from you upon my lack.
Blessed is he who came and was baptized by his own servant, as was fitting for him;
he who sanctified baptism—to him be glory."
Here ends the homily on the baptism of our Saviour by John.
On Holy Baptism

Also by the holy Mar Jacob. Homily 9, on holy baptism.
O Son, who made us sons to your Father from within the waters,
through you I will speak of your spiritual birth.

Only-Begotten, who gave us his Spirit in baptism,
give me a word with which to sing to you lovingly.
Lord, who willed to become a brother to wicked servants,
fill me with your teaching, that I may proclaim your goodness every day.
Great Sun, who let his light dwell within the waters,
let me be illumined, and I will tell of your beauty as I marvel.
Son of the Virgin, who gave us a virgin mother too,
let my words bring you forth with discernment as I marvel.
In the stirring of the mind, let my tongue proclaim a homily of praise
without confusion, its voice free of dispute.
Let baptism be the occasion for the story I have begun,
and let the homily go on to the assembly of the Only-Begotten's praise.
May this mother, who every day gives birth to the immortal,
stir my words, so that your stories may go forth and flow out to the world.
The daughter of light, who gives birth to embodied suns,
has called me today: "Come, let us delight in her savours."
The mother of life, whose children are cast forth out of darkness,
has asked a homily of me, and if I neglect it, that would be a wrong.
The King's bride has made a wedding feast for the whole world:
peoples and world, come to the banquet of Christ!

She has opened living waters from the Father's house to the world:
O all who thirst, drink hope from her spring!
Who is this, to whom the peoples of the earth are gathered,
and who hands out to them garments of light to clothe them?
Who is this bride who has come up from within the waters,
and is like a crown of [?], the choicest of all [?]?
Who is this, whose beauty the River Jordan feared,
and prepared before her a bridal chamber and waves, that she might be wedded in it?
Who is this glorious one who sits within the spring
and bears children to become brothers to the Son of God?
Who is this, before whom the priests and ministers of the earth stand,
who feed from her and hallow her with their hovering?
Who [?] that is without limit? Who
is this who leans upon the Only-Begotten,
steeped in his blood and embracing him, to rejoice with him?
Who is this who draws a man toward the spring,
and mingles fire and Spirit in the waters to give them to drink?

Who is this whose appearance is like a cloud of light,
who by her beauty holily captivates everyone who comes?
Who is this who at once opened her lofty gates
and shut Sheol, which had stood open upon the generations?
Who is this new mother who takes up the old and goes into labour with them,
so that by birth they may become children?
Who is this nurse within the waters,
weaving a garment of light for all who come to her?
Who is this, lady of glory and full of radiance,
to whom all creation runs to rejoice with her?
Baptism is the daughter of day, who opened her gates,
and night fled, which was hateful; [?] she labours to give birth,
and the Only-Begotten sustains her by the Spirit of his Father.
She is the betrothed of the Sun by whom all creation is lit,
and the world grazes lovingly in the meadows of her light.
Baptism is the gate that opens into the kingdom,
and through it a man enters toward God, to be with him.
Baptism is a new ship that carries the dead;
in her they are revived and cross over to the place of the immortals.

Baptism is set between world and world,
and through her a man enters from death into the place of life.
On this side of baptism is the gate of Sheol,
and beyond her the gate that opens into Paradise.
In baptism the Cross is set up like a ladder,
and it carries man from within the waters to the height above.
Baptism is a bridge fastened between the two banks,
and except by her no one crosses over to God.
Baptism is a womb that every day gives birth to the living
and sanctifies them to be brothers to the Only-Begotten.
Baptism gives back to Adam the robe of glory
which the serpent had stolen from him among the trees.
Baptism is a great furnace full of light,
and in it men are cast anew to become immortal.
Baptism is the great highway to the house of the kingdom,
and it leads whoever walks on it to the place of light.
In baptism the treasures of God's house are laid up,
and whoever enters finds riches without limit.
Baptism gives birth every day in her virginity:
